setup.title: Welcome to AIRAG
setup.ollamaTitle: Local AI isn't set up yet
setup.intro: Choose the AI that reads the pages and writes your articles. You can change this any time in Settings.
setup.missingKey: AIRAG is set to use {p}, but no API key was found. Add one below or switch to a local model.
setup.localDesc: Free and private. Runs on your own PC, so it needs a reasonably powerful computer.
setup.cloudDesc: Fast and high quality. Needs an API key from the provider and costs a little per search.
setup.ollamaMissing: Ollama isn't installed on this PC.
setup.ollamaHow: Install it, then come back here. AIRAG starts it automatically and helps you download a model.
setup.ollamaInstalled: Ollama is installed but not running.
setup.noModels: No models downloaded yet. After setup, open Settings → AI model to download one.
setup.searchKeysDesc: DuckDuckGo works without a key but can be rate-limited. A free Brave Search key gives more reliable results.
setup.later: You can change everything later in Settings.
set.title: Settings
set.generalIntro: Language, window mode, updates and storage.
set.appearanceIntro: Theme, colour palette and accent colour. Changes apply right away.
set.modelIntro: Local models through Ollama, or cloud models with your own API key.
set.searchIntro: Where AIRAG looks things up. DuckDuckGo works out of the box; Brave, Google or SearXNG give more and better results.
set.promptsIntro: Change how the research agent writes. Safety rules, the answer language and source citations are always kept.
set.fetchIntro: How pages are opened and turned into text.
set.researchIntro: How hard AIRAG digs before it decides between results, an article, or suggestions.
gen.answerHelp: The language articles and summaries are written in.
gen.windowHelp: Desktop mode shows AIRAG in its own window. Browser mode opens it in your web browser and keeps an icon in the system tray.
model.loaded: {n} models available. Click the model field to choose one.
ollama.ram: This PC has {n} GB of memory.
ollama.deleteConfirm: Delete {m}? You can download it again later.
ollama.tooBig: Probably too big for this PC
lib.title: Library
lib.intro: Retrieve & Get: let AIRAG search your own notes and documents, for example an Obsidian vault or a folder of PDFs. Files are indexed on this computer; only short excerpts are sent to the AI model.
fetch.browserMissing: Not installed. Only needed for sites that load their text with JavaScript.
f.p.autostart: Start Ollama automatically when AIRAG needs it
h.llm.temperature: Lower is more factual and consistent.
f.app.check_updates: Check for updates when AIRAG starts
h.app.history_limit: Older searches are deleted automatically to save space.
h.app.port: If it's busy, a free port is picked automatically. 0 = always pick a free one.
h.search.region: auto = based on your answer language. Or a code like us-en, uk-en, no-no, de-de, wt-wt (worldwide).
f.library.web_too: Also search the web when 'My library' is ticked
h.library.web_too: Turn off to answer only from your own files.
f.library.trust: Default reliability of your own files (0-10)
h.library.trust: The AI still judges each file. Personal notes are useful but not independently checked.
h.prompts.custom_instructions: Added to articles, summaries and explainers. For example: 'Always use metric units' or 'Explain it like I'm a nurse'.
h.prompts.planner_instructions: Added to the search planner. For example: 'Include Norwegian sources' or 'Avoid Reddit'.
h.prompts.article_prompt: Replaces the main article instructions. Leave empty to use the default.
f.research.passage_chars: Text per page sent to the AI (characters)
f.research.min_findings: Min findings to write an article
f.research.enough_findings: Stop searching after this many findings
pclink.title: Share with my phone
pclink.intro: Lets the AIRAG phone app use the Ollama models on this PC over your home Wi-Fi. Only model requests are shared, and the phone needs the pairing code.
pclink.onHelp: Keep AIRAG and Ollama running on this PC while you use the phone.
pclink.offHelp: Turn it on to get an address and pairing code for the phone app.
pclink.newCodeHelp: Phones using the old code will be disconnected
pclink.newCodeConfirm: Make a new pairing code? Phones using the old one will need the new code.
pclink.noNetwork: No network found. Is this PC connected to Wi-Fi or a cable?
pclink.steps: On the phone: Settings → AI model → My PC (Ollama), then paste the address and code. If Windows asks about network access, allow it for private networks. Start Ollama on this PC first (above).
pclink.internet: Allow connections from outside my home network
pclink.internetHelp: Off by default. Only turn on if you've set up port forwarding and understand the risk; the pairing code is then the only protection.
h.pc_link.base_url: Shown on your PC under Settings → AI model → Share with my phone, e.g. 192.168.1.20:47120
log.title: Log
log.copyFailed: Couldn't copy. Select the text instead.
log.help: Shows the latest activity from AIRAG's log. API keys and pairing codes are hidden, so you can paste it into a bug report.
src.suspicious: This page contained text that tried to give the AI instructions. It was removed and the source's reliability lowered.
lib.needFolder: Add a folder first (for example your Obsidian vault), then tick My library to search it too.
repair.appSource: Running from source code, nothing to check
repair.appSkipped: Can't be checked for this version
repair.settingsBad: Can't be read. Repair keeps a copy and goes back to the defaults.
repair.libraryBad: Damaged. Repair rebuilds it from your folders.
repair.historyBad: {n} can't be opened. Repair moves them aside.
repair.reinstallHelp: Downloads this version again from GitHub and reinstalls it. Settings, history and library stay.
repair.reinstallConfirm: Download and reinstall this version of AIRAG? Your settings, history and library are kept.
step.reuse.done: Using {n} sources from the previous search
step.reuse.run: Using {n} sources from the previous search
date.tip: Only show results from a period of time
run.againTip: Runs a new search and also uses the sources found here. This search stays in your history.
save.tip: Save this article to My library as a Markdown file with its sources
my.title: My library
my.intro: Where saved articles and files you add are kept. It can be on any drive and is always searched when My library is ticked.
my.notYet: Created when you save your first article
my.moveConfirm: Move the files you pick into My library? They'll be removed from where they are now.
my.addedCopied: Added {n} files (some apps only allow copying, so those originals were kept)
saved.title: Saved articles
saved.empty: No saved articles yet. Use Save on an article to keep it in My library.
save.rich: Include pictures and the interactive explainer
save.richHelp: Pictures are stored inside the saved copy so they work offline. Larger files.
save.richHelpNoInter: Pictures are stored inside the saved copy so they work offline; open the interactive explainer first to include it too. Larger files.
save.sourceTip: Save a light, text-only copy of this page to My library
tr.help: The AI translates naturally, keeping expressions, citations and numbers intact.
tr.tip: Pick a language, and the AI translates this page naturally (not word for word)
upd.title: AIRAG {v} is available
upd.youHave: You have version {v}. Here's what's new:
upd.skipTip: Don't ask again until a newer version comes out
upd.permission: Allow AIRAG to install apps on the screen that opened; the update installs when you come back.
mic.denied: AIRAG needs microphone access for this. Allow it in your device settings.
mic.error: Speech input isn't working right now.
extras.label: Pictures & explainer
extras.tip: Look for pictures and check whether an interactive explainer fits. Untick to use fewer AI tokens.
inter.checkNow: This search skipped the explainer check. Tap to check now whether one would help.
tab.general.tip: Language, window mode and history size
tab.model.tip: Which AI to use, Ollama models and sharing with your phone
tab.search.tip: Search engine, region and safe search
tab.library.tip: My library and the folders AIRAG may search
tab.research.tip: How deep each search goes and how pages are read
tab.prompts.tip: Writing style, length, your own instructions and explainer detail
tab.system.tip: This device, updates, repair, backups and logs
sys.intro: What AIRAG runs on, plus updates, storage and maintenance.
sys.cacheHelp: Forgets pages read during searches and reloads the app's screens. Use it if something looks outdated after an update.
sys.backupHelp: Export settings, defaults and history to a file in My library/Backups, or import one.
sys.backupKeys: Include API keys (keep that file private)
sys.importConfirm: Import a backup? Its settings replace the current ones, and its searches are added to your history.
def.intro: What new searches start with. You can still change these for a single search on the home page.
h.defaults.library: Tick My library on the home page by default.
h.defaults.extras: Look for pictures and check whether an interactive explainer fits. Turn off to use fewer AI tokens.
f.defaults.save_rich: Save articles with pictures and the explainer
h.prompts.explainer_level: Simple uses the fewest tokens; detailed makes richer simulations and games but costs more.
lic.summary: AIRAG is free and open source under the MIT license.
lic.can: You may use it for anything, including at work, and copy, change and share it, also inside your own projects.
lic.must: Copies and changed versions must keep the copyright notice and this license text.
lic.not: You can't remove the copyright notice or claim you wrote the original, and it comes without any warranty.
lic.name: The AIRAG name and logo aren't covered: give modified versions your own name and logo.
upd.testUpToDate: This is a test build (pre-release). Latest release: {v}
run.cancelTip: Stop this search. Leaving the page doesn't stop it; it keeps going in the background.
run.queued: Waiting for {n} earlier search(es) to finish…
tab.usage.tip: Tokens and cost per AI model, and your monthly budget
usage.intro: How many tokens AIRAG has used this month and what it cost, per AI model. Local models (Ollama) are free and only count tokens.
usage.unpriced: Some models have no known price, so their cost isn't counted.
usage.prices: Prices from OpenRouter's public list, updated {when}.
usage.pricesBuiltIn: Using built-in prices (the online price list couldn't be loaded).
h.usage.monthly_budget: Shown as a bar above. 0 = no budget.
f.usage.tell_model: Tell the AI when the budget is nearly used
h.usage.tell_model: When 70% is used, the AI is asked to search less and write shorter answers.
f.usage.stop_at_budget: Stop new AI work when the budget is used up
inter.background: You can close this. It keeps building in the background.
inter.queuedTip: Waiting for another explainer to finish…
inter.buildingTip: Building in the background. Click to watch it.
aud.title: Customize audio
aud.intro: Sound effects for the microphone and for finished or failed searches and explainers. Use your own clips if you like.
aud.masterHelp: AIRAG's own volume for all sound effects.
aud.masterPhoneHelp: This is your phone's media volume (the music note). Changing it here changes it on the phone too.
aud.resetHelp: Only applied when you press Save. Cancel keeps your current sounds.
aud.tooBig: Sound files can be at most 3 MB.
aud.newClip: New clip: {f} (saved when you press Save)
aud.resetDone: Defaults restored here. Press Save to keep them, or Cancel to undo.
tts.title: Read aloud
tts.intro: Have articles read aloud with your device's voices. More voices can be installed in your phone's or computer's speech settings.
tts.voiceHelp: Female and male pick the best matching voice for the article's language. Or pick a specific voice.
tts.sample: Hello! This is how AIRAG sounds when it reads an article aloud.
pin.tip: Pin this article to the top of the home page
pin.title: Pinned
exp.tip: Save the article (and its explainer) as one web page file that opens in any browser, offline, without AIRAG. Good for sending to someone.
exp.noExplainer: This article's explainer hasn't been built yet, so it isn't included. Build it first to add it.
exp.help: Pictures and the explainer are packed inside the file. Send it to anyone: it opens in a browser, even offline.
art.copyFailed: Couldn't copy. Select the text and copy it instead.
f.defaults.speech_autosearch: Search as soon as you stop speaking
h.defaults.speech_autosearch: After speaking into the microphone, the search starts by itself. Off: check or edit the text first.
f.library.min_relevance: Minimum relevance to use a library file (1-10)
h.library.min_relevance: Library files the AI rates below this for the question are left out and not listed.
exp.intro: Choose what goes into the web page file. Parts that haven't been made yet are made first (this uses some AI tokens).
exp.willMake: Will be written first (a few AI tokens)
exp.willBuild: Will be built first (uses AI tokens, can take a minute)
exp.picturesNote: Packed into the file (makes it bigger)
more.tip: Search for more sources and add what they say to this article, without rewriting it
more.added: Added {n} new sources to the article
more.none: No new useful sources found. The article is unchanged.
pinsrc.pinned: Source pinned. It's on the home page until you unpin it.
pinsrc.title: Pinned sources
pinsrc.unpinConfirm: Unpin this source? Its saved copy is deleted.
btns.title: Buttons shown
btns.intro: Hide tool buttons you don't use, so pages stay tidy. Everything is shown by default.
h.research.use_pinned: Pinned pages that match the question are read from their saved copy (no download) and can be cited.
h.defaults.pinned_view: Saved page: the copy saved when you pinned it. AI version: a short version written by the AI, focused on your search.
tab.tools.tip: Show or hide the tool buttons on articles, results and sources
more.tipResults: Search for more sources and add them to these results
more.addedResults: Added {n} new sources to the results
wiki.title: Wikis
wiki.intro: Searched next to the search engine. Wikipedia uses your answer language. Add any MediaWiki-based wiki (Fandom, PsychonautWiki, the Minecraft wiki...) by its address.
wiki.aboutPh: What it's good for (helps the AI choose)
wiki.already: That wiki is already in the list.
wiki.added: Added {name}. Press Save to keep it.
h.search.use_wikis: Searches Wikipedia (in your answer language) and any wikis you add, next to the search engine.
h.research.favourite_sites: Comma separated, same rules as blocked sites. Pages from these start with a higher trust score.
h.research.skip_domains: Comma separated. Never read. A site name covers all its subdomains; add a path (site.com/forum) to block only that directory and everything below it.
h.fetch.youtube: Reads a video's title, description and, when YouTube allows it, its captions, so it can be used as a source.
h.fetch.youtube_retries: How many times to try again when YouTube doesn't answer.
f.research.explainer_examples: Explainers: look up code examples first
h.research.explainer_examples: Before building an interactive explainer, a quick web search finds code for similar simulations to learn from.
rt.label: Research tools
rt.askPh: Ask a follow-up about this article…
rt.compareTip: Compare the main options or viewpoints in the article side by side
rt.timelineTip: Put the events in the article in date order
rt.factcheckTip: Check the selected text (or the article's main claims) against the sources and the web
rt.rewriteTip: Rewrite the selected paragraph. You see the new version next to the old one before anything changes.
rt.calcTip: Solve the selected formula or sum
rt.citeTip: Copy the sources as APA, MLA or BibTeX
rt.voiceTip: Say what to do with the selected text
rt.elaborateQ: How was this worked out, and how does it relate to the article?
rt.selectFirst: Select the text to rewrite first.
rt.selectMath: Select a formula or sum first.
rt.empty: Ask a follow-up, or select text in the article for more options. Answers show up here.
rw.title: Rewrite
rw.ph: How should it change? For example: simpler, shorter, more formal
rw.hint: Say how to change it, or just press Rewrite.
cite.title: Cite sources
h.defaults.citation_style: Used by Cite and Copy with source.
atools.title: What the AI may use
atools.intro: Tools the AI can call while it answers, for example the calculator. Each kind of agent has its own set.
atools.standardHelp: Answers follow-up questions and toolbar actions. It can't ask for more tools; without one, it works it out in text.
atools.autonomousHelp: The research agent coming in 0.5. It may ask you once per session to allow a tool for itself or its sub-agents.
atools.subagentsHelp: Helpers the autonomous agent starts for parts of a task (0.5).
tool.calculator.help: Exact maths, equations, algebra and statistics. Free (no AI tokens).
tool.datetime.help: Today's date and the time. Free.
tool.search_sources.help: Looks through the pages AIRAG already read. Free.
tool.web_search.help: New searches for fact-checks and follow-ups. Uses the network.
tool.read_page.help: Reads a page found by web search. Uses tokens.
tool.read_aloud.help: Speaks text with your device's voice. Free.
tool.locate_more_sources.help: Same as the button. Uses about as many tokens as a short search.
tool.copy.help: Copies an exact quote or result for you.
usage.localCompare: Your local (Ollama) use would have cost about {v} on {model}.
effort.title: Quality or saving
effort.intro: Choose how much each kind of agent spends on an answer. Saving modes use fewer words, fewer searches and fewer tool calls; quality modes read more sources and check more.
effort.minimalHelp: Fewest tokens: very short answers, about a third of the research rounds, tools only when needed.
effort.saverHelp: Short answers and fewer sources and tool calls.
effort.mediumHelp: The default balance of quality and tokens.
effort.detailedHelp: Longer answers, about a third more research rounds and sources, more cross-checking.
effort.maxHelp: Most thorough: the most sources, rounds and tool calls. Uses the most tokens.
img.buttonTip: Let the AI look at a picture or screenshot (you can also paste or drop one here)
img.ph: What do you want to know? (optional)
img.hint: Ask a question, or just press Analyze. Formulas are written out and solved; other pictures are described.
img.badFile: That file couldn't be opened as a picture.
img.noVision: The selected AI model can't look at pictures. Choose a vision model in Settings, or use an image-to-text or maths-scanner app.
img.apps: Tip: an image-to-text or maths-scanner app can turn the picture into text you can paste into AIRAG.
rt.elaborateQ2: Elaborate on this: explain it in more depth and how it connects to the article and its sources.
f.library.reopen_to_history: Reopened saved articles go back in History
h.library.reopen_to_history: So follow-ups and the other toolbar tools work on them.
sumfile.tip: A small file with the summary and the sources' links (saved in My library/Summaries)
open.hint: Markdown or text, a saved article (.airag.json) or an exported web page
open.tooBig: That file is too big to open (over 20 MB).
open.reread: Updated from your changes to the saved .md file
open.noAI: Opened from a file, without the AI
h.usage.stop_at_budget: Searches, follow-ups, rewrites, explainers, summaries, translations and image analysis. Work that's already running finishes.
inter.navBlocked: The explainer tried to open a web page, so it was stopped. Explainers stay offline.
f.research.explainer_local_examples: Explainers: learn from code in My library
h.research.explainer_local_examples: JavaScript in your own library files that matches the explainer can be used as a reference. Nothing is fetched from the web.
f.research.explainer_web_examples: Explainers: look up code examples on the web
h.research.explainer_web_examples: Only used when your search itself is about programming. Code from the web can hide instructions or mistakes, so it's off by default.
regen.title: Regenerate article
regen.intro: Writes the article again from the same sources. The current version is kept, so you can go back to it.
regen.ph: For example: shorter, simpler, more about the history…
regen.keepHelp: Paragraphs you rewrote and answers you added stay as they are.
regen.cost: About as many tokens as writing the article once
regen.noVersions: No changes yet. Every regeneration, rewrite and added answer will be listed here.
regen.keptNote: Undo and Restore never delete anything: every version stays in this list (the last 20 are kept).
